Event calendars and optional sync

Read events, then choose when to sync.

Understand Mac calendar viewing, permission and explicit two-way synchronization.

Optional on Mac 1.5.15 build31 · Unavailable on Windows 1.5.13
OverviewHow to useExampleScope and limitsRelated features

Viewing and syncing are separate

Mac shows events from the selected connection in a monthly calendar with date details. The compact menu bar panel shows up to three connected events for today. This is separate from the arrival-record calendar.

Calendar is an optional plugin; basic attendance does not require it. Reading events differs from adding or updating events between accounts. The Daouoffice plugin’s server lookup is also separate and does not start two-way sync merely by fetching events.

Connect and review first

  1. Install and enable Calendar in Settings → Plugin management.
  2. In Calendar settings, use Open Internet Accounts to connect your own Google and DaouOffice accounts through macOS Internet Accounts.
  3. Choose Allow calendar access and grant full calendar access in macOS. The first event lookup also requires read access; permission only to add events cannot read them.
  4. Choose the calendars to display in the Daouoffice calendar and Google calendar selectors. Empty selections show no events.
  5. Open the event view and choose Refresh events to read the selected calendars. Stop here if you only want to view events.
  6. For two-way sync, select test calendars from different accounts, confirm their account connections, then review additions, held events and conflicts in Preview first sync.
  7. Explicitly choose Start two-way sync after reviewing. Resume a paused connection only after a fresh preview.

macOS Internet Accounts manages login and credentials for this system-calendar connection. Granting access, selecting calendars and refreshing do not start HappyLulu’s two-way event writes. A preview also leaves events unchanged; additions and edits require you to explicitly start sync after review.

From viewing to syncing

Reading a 14:00 meeting in the app is a lookup. To copy it to another account’s test calendar, review the copy direction and any holds in the preview, then start synchronization.

Recurring events are copied as individual occurrences from 30 days before through 365 days after today. Invitations become personal copies without re-inviting attendees, and the original is protected. Ordinary display reminders are preserved.

Permission, conflicts and server confirmation

Reading system-calendar events also requires authorized read access. Grant full calendar access and select calendars to display. Permission only to add events cannot support viewing or two-way sync. Conflicting edits on both sides are not overwritten automatically. Deletions do not propagate automatically. Out-of-range recurrences and special alarms are held with a reason.

Fetch failures are distinguished from no events. If you see a connection or range warning, check settings and refresh. Half-day title recognition is a separate optional feature; manual workday choices take priority.

A successful local macOS calendar save is separate from confirmation on both web servers. Check the actual web calendars separately. External connections communicate with servers. Windows 1.5.13 has no calendar, plugin or sync features.
